implementation_plan: Keep Speed Dot v1 as a singleton owned by LevelManager: add a speedDotState object with enabled, active, x, y, r, spawnedAt, nextSpawnAt, targetOnion, boostDurationMs, boostSpeedMultiplier, and spawn delay ranges from defaults.

Add LevelManager default tuning locally: enabled true, radius about 9-11, boostDurationMs 3000, boostSpeedMultiplier 1.35, firstSpawnDelayMsRange [5000,8000], respawnDelayMsRange [6000,10000], maxActive 1, onionCandidateLimit 1. Do not add UI or asset references.
If config is used, add only an optional top-level speedDot object in config/levels.json and preserve absent-field defaults. Do not add per-wave churn unless later tuning proves it necessary.

Reset Speed Dot in LevelManager.clearLevel/loadLevel. On reset, clear target on all current onions before dropping the array if practical, then create a fresh inactive dot state with nextSpawnAt based on the new frame time or lazy-initialized first update.

Add LevelManager.updateSpeedDot(now): initialize nextSpawnAt if missing, spawn a dot when inactive and now >= nextSpawnAt, constrain spawn position with arena.constrainCircle(dot.x,dot.y,dot.r), and assign exactly one target onion if active.

Dot spawn should use bounded random positions inside world with arena containment. For v1, avoid broad safe-zone rules; optionally reject positions within roughly player.r + dot.r + 40 of the player for immediate pickup prevention if implemented in a small bounded retry loop.
Add LevelManager.getSpeedDot() returning either null or a read-only/copy-like active dot view needed by main.js draw/collision. Main.js must not mutate dot state directly.

Add LevelManager.consumeSpeedDot(now, collector): if active, clear active and targetOnion, clear all onion dot targets, set nextSpawnAt using respawn range, and return true. If inactive, return false. This is the single atomic consume gate.

Add LevelManager.assignSpeedDotTarget(): filter onions by alive, not dying, and onion.canTargetSpeedDot(now). Pick nearest to dot. Assign only that onion by onion.setSpeedDotTarget(dot), clear all others. If all are in chase or dying, no onion target is assigned and Pi-chan can still collect the dot.

Add Player boost API: applySpeedBoost(multiplier,durationMs,now) returns false if already boosted; isSpeedBoosted(now); getMovementSpeed(now). Do not mutate this.speed. Player.update uses getMovementSpeed(now) for x/y movement; Player.shoot keeps this.speed * BULLET_SPEED_FACTOR so bullet speed is intentionally unaffected.

Add Onion boost/target API: applySpeedBoost(multiplier,durationMs,now), isSpeedBoosted(now), getMovementSpeed(now), canTargetSpeedDot(now), setSpeedDotTarget(dot), clearSpeedDotTarget(). Do not add a base class or generic effect manager.

Modify Onion #setVelocityFromDirection to use getMovementSpeed(frameNow) or a current effective speed value. Because #setVelocityFromDirection is private and currently has no now parameter, prefer storing this.frameNow at update start or adding a private #getMovementSpeed() based on performance.now fallback. Keep the diff local.

Modify Onion.update: after updateOnionAI, if state is CHASE_PICHAN clearSpeedDotTarget and continue existing chase path. If non-chase and speedDotTarget is active, move toward dot using dominant axis, existing direction names, #setVelocityFromDirection, and #applyArenaConstraint(true/false as appropriate). This replaces random movement for the assigned candidate only.

Keep chase dominant over dot targeting. Onions in CHASE_PICHAN must never abandon Pi-chan for dot. A boosted onion that later enters chase can keep the temporary boost as a final movement multiplier until expiry, but it must not target the dot while chasing.
In main.js, add a local circle overlap helper for dot pickup; do not change js/core/physics.js unless impact review explicitly prefers a shared helper.

In main.js update loop, after onions = levelManager.getOnions(), call levelManager.updateSpeedDot(now) so spawn/target state follows cleanup and replacement spawns. Then run Speed Dot pickup collision after bullet->player game-over and before onion->player lethal collision.

For pickup resolution, compute overlapping eligible collectors among Pi-chan and the assigned onion only. Choose the nearest overlapping collector to the dot; tie-break to Pi-chan for deterministic control feel. Call applySpeedBoost first; only consume the dot if the boost was accepted. This enforces no-stack without deleting a dot under an already-boosted subject.
For onion pickup, only the assigned target onion may collect in v1. Other non-chase onions overlapping the dot do not collect unless they are the current candidate, preserving one onion candidate.
Draw Speed Dot in main.js within the arena clip before onions and player. Use simple canvas circles/ring/pulse with high contrast. Do not add assets, CSS, HUD text, or numeric timers.

Add Player/Onion boost feedback inside existing draw methods: a small ring/glow or saturation change gated by isSpeedBoosted(now). Onion feedback must be readable in chase without looking like the existing red chase flash; prefer cyan/white rim or yellow-white ring rather than red.
Do not modify scoring, bullets, wave cap/budget/cadence, arena motion, online services, nickname, lifecycle, audio, CSS, assets, HUD, README, or docs in the build patch.

The first dot appears after a randomized 5-8 second delay; after pickup, respawn delay is randomized 6-10 seconds.
Speed Dot is collectible by Pi-chan or the single assigned onion candidate. Other onions cannot collect it in v1.
Pi-chan and onion receive identical boostDurationMs and boostSpeedMultiplier when pickup succeeds.
No stacking: a subject already boosted cannot receive another boost and must not consume a newly spawned dot.

manual_tests: Start ./serve.sh and open http://127.0.0.1:8080. Wave 1 should start normally with no console errors and no dot before the configured first delay.
Wait 5-8 seconds in Wave 1. Expected: exactly one Speed Dot appears inside the arena clip, readable over the background.
Collect dot with Pi-chan. Expected: dot disappears immediately, Pi-chan moves faster for about 3 seconds, visual feedback appears, bullet speed/range feel unchanged, then normal speed returns.
While Pi-chan is boosted, shoot repeatedly. Expected: bullets do not become faster than baseline and onion chase speed does not jump because player.speed remained base.

Let an onion collect the dot. Expected: only the nearest non-chase onion targets it, dot disappears on pickup, that onion gets the same duration/multiplier feedback, and normal speed returns after expiry.

With at least two onions, shoot while the assigned onion is targeting the dot. Expected: assigned onion enters chase, stops targeting the dot, continues chasing Pi-chan, and another non-chase onion is assigned if available.
Force all alive onions into CHASE_PICHAN while dot is active. Expected: no onion moves toward the dot; Pi-chan can still collect it.
Move Pi-chan and assigned onion into near-simultaneous overlap with the dot. Expected: exactly one collector receives boost and the dot consumes once, using the documented nearest/tie-break rule.
Keep playing after pickup. Expected: no second dot appears until respawn delay; never more than one dot is active.
Kill onions and complete Wave 1/2. Expected: wave cap, replacement cadence, score, bullet kills, and level transition remain unchanged.
Use Play Again, Continue, and window.goto/pi goto flow. Expected: active dot, target assignment, and boost state do not leak across reset or level change.
Visual check desktop/mobile sizes. Expected: dot and boost feedback are readable but do not overlap HUD or add numeric UI.

risks: Bullet-speed regression: mutating Player.speed would buff bullets and onion AI speed. Mitigation: Player boost uses movement getter only; shoot() keeps base speed.
Onion boost lost or stale: OnionAI overwrites onion.speed. Mitigation: onion boost is final multiplier at velocity calculation, not persistent speed assignment.

Target oscillation: nearest onion can switch every frame when distances are close. Mitigation: v1 can accept mild reassignment, or keep current target while still eligible unless another onion is meaningfully closer; do not add complex hysteresis unless observed.
Collision ordering ambiguity: simultaneous pickup could double-apply. Mitigation: main.js computes one winner and LevelManager.consumeSpeedDot is atomic.
Chase conflict: assigned onion may enter chase after shooting. Mitigation: Onion.update clears/ignores dot target whenever state is CHASE_PICHAN; LevelManager reassigns next update.
Spawn unfairness: dot can spawn too close to Pi-chan or edge. Mitigation: use arena.constrainCircle and optional small retry safe distance from player only, no broad placement system.
Visual confusion: boosted chase onion could look like existing chase feedback. Mitigation: non-red ring/glow for boost and keep chase red readable.
Scope creep: generic power-up/effect framework would exceed v1. Mitigation: singleton LevelManager state and narrow Player/Onion APIs only.
deferred_items: HUD timers, counters, numeric UI, scoring/combo changes
New assets, sounds, CSS, or sprite variants
Pathfinding/steering/hysteresis beyond a minimal nearest-target rule
Documentation updates outside final build/report if requested later

Bullet-player collision must remain before Speed Dot pickup so a lethal self-hit cannot be masked by collecting the dot.

regression_risks: Highest risk: accidental Player.speed mutation would increase bullet speed and indirectly increase OnionAI speed through player.speed. Approval requires a movement-speed getter or equivalent base-speed separation while shoot() and OnionAI still see baseline Player.speed.

Second risk: onion boost being overwritten or left stale when OnionAI/chase rewrites onion.speed. Approval requires final multiplier application at velocity calculation, including random, dot-target, and chase movement paths.

Collision risk: simultaneous overlaps must resolve through one deterministic winner and one atomic consume call. consumeSpeedDot must be the single state transition from active to inactive and must clear onion targets.

No-stack edge case: an already boosted subject must not consume a newly spawned dot. If multiple collectors overlap and the nearest/tie-break winner cannot accept a boost, build should either leave the dot active or choose the next explicitly eligible collector; it must not consume without applying a boost.
Targeting risk: only the assigned nearest alive non-dying non-CHASE_PICHAN onion may pursue or collect. CHASE_PICHAN must clear/ignore dot target every frame it applies.

Lifecycle risk: reset, Continue, goto, level transition, and config reload must clear active dot, target references, and boost state. LevelManager reset plus fresh entities is sufficient if no globals are introduced.
Wave regression risk is low if Speed Dot state remains separate from waveState and updateWave/isWaveComplete are not modified beyond call ordering in main.js.
